source.title: Northern Whig, 18 May 1949, p. 4 ("Nominations for County and Rural Councils": Dungannon); Belfast News-Letter, 18 May 1949, p. 7
source.publisher: Northern Whig (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: returned unopposed: the only nomination for Crosdernott (printed 'Crosdernott') in the Northern Whig's list of all nineteen Dungannon rural divisions, read on the BNA page image and keyed twice from two different crops (no differences); Meenagh is the only division with two names. The Belfast News-Letter of the same day reports retiring members nominated in seventeen divisions, two new members (Bernagh, Granville) and the Meenagh contest as the only one.

note: Triennial election of the 19 electoral divisions of Dungannon rural district, one member each, polled on 2 June 1949. Nominations closed on 17 May 1949; the Northern Whig (18 May 1949, p. 4) prints the nominee for every division. Eighteen divisions had a single nomination; the only contest was at Meenagh, between F. M'Grath and A. P. M'Grath, whose result has not been found. No party labels are printed. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Crossdernott' to Crossdernot (13 Nov 2026, by the owner's rule for division spellings: the official or DED-map name where there is one, otherwise the spelling most rounds use): the 1948 order naming Dungannon Rural District's nineteen divisions (Ministry of Health and Local Government, 26 August 1948; Belfast Gazette, 1 April 1949), the 1911 and 1930 DED maps (CROSSDERNOT) and the OSNI townland spell it Crossdernot. This round was filed under the spelling 'Crossdernott', a form of the division's name it keeps as an alias; the old address (crossdernott) answers with a redirect to this one.
